rules.explanation: Liability is not capped, or the counterparty is excluded from damages while we are not.
rules.recommendation: Require a mutual cap (e.g. 12 months of fees) and a mutual exclusion of consequential damages.

match: arising out of or relating to
rules.explanation: Indemnity is one-sided and uncapped rather than limited to specific third-party claims.
rules.recommendation: Make indemnities mutual and scope them to third-party claims (IP infringement, data breach, gross negligence).

match: may terminate this agreement at any time
rules.explanation: The counterparty can terminate for convenience on short notice while our termination rights are restricted.
rules.recommendation: Make termination-for-convenience mutual with at least 60-90 days notice and transition assistance.

rules.explanation: The agreement renews automatically; missing the notice window locks in another term.
rules.recommendation: Add a renewal reminder to the contract calendar or require an affirmative renewal order.

rules.explanation: Fees can change unilaterally without a cap.
rules.recommendation: Fix fees for the initial term and cap annual increases (e.g. CPI or 3-5%).

rules.explanation: Payment window is shorter than the standard net-30/45, or late interest is above market.
rules.recommendation: Negotiate net-45 payment terms and late interest no higher than 1% per month.

rules.explanation: The counterparty may use or share our data beyond what is needed to deliver the service.
rules.recommendation: Limit processing to documented instructions, add breach notification (72h) and deletion on termination.

rules.explanation: Work can be subcontracted without notice, so we cannot vet who handles our data or deliverables.
rules.recommendation: Require prior written consent for subcontractors and flow down confidentiality and security terms.

rules.explanation: Forum or governing law differs from the approved list (Oregon, Delaware) or mandates exclusive arbitration.
rules.recommendation: Prefer Oregon or Delaware law; allow injunctive relief in court.

rules.explanation: Obligations are framed as effort rather than measurable commitments.
rules.recommendation: Add measurable service levels with service credits or termination rights for chronic failure.
